content: The process of bone mineralization and bone accumulation is particularly critical during periods of growth. Engaging in high-impact exercise has been demonstrated to play a significant role in preventing the onset of osteoporosis. However, in individuals with poor nutritional status, such as those suffering from anorexia nervosa or celiac disease, high-impact exercise may negatively affect bone mineralization. A diet rich in calcium and vitamin D is essential for preventing bone loss. Patients who are at an elevated risk of developing osteoporosis, such as those undergoing chronic steroid therapy, are typically treated with vitamin D and calcium supplementation. In cases of renal disease, more active forms of vitamin D, such as 1,25-dihydroxycholecalciferol (calcitriol), are utilized because the kidneys are unable to efficiently convert calcidiol (25-hydroxycholecalciferol), the storage form of vitamin D, into calcitriol. Smoking cessation is an effective measure to prevent osteoporosis as well as other associated diseases. Limiting alcohol consumption to moderate levels, defined as one to two alcoholic beverages per day, is also recommended. Additionally, minimizing the use of medications known to contribute to osteoporosis, such as anticonvulsants or corticosteroids, by prescribing the lowest effective dosages, can help mitigate the risk of bone loss.
